questions.stem: Click events must be filtered and sent to two destinations, an eventhouse and a lakehouse, and the team wants to set it up without writing code. Which fits?

options.text: An eventstream, with a filter in the event processor and two destinations
A pipeline copy activity scheduled every minute for each destination
A Spark Structured Streaming notebook that writes to both destinations
A KQL update policy that copies each row into the lakehouse

questions.explanation: Eventstreams bring real-time events into Fabric, transform them and send them to various destinations without writing any code. The event processor is a drag-and-drop editor for processing, transforming and routing.

questions.stem: Operators want to explore streaming data interactively with a query language and see results seconds after it's ingested. Which engine fits?

options.text: A Spark Structured Streaming job that writes CSV files every hour
A warehouse table loaded once a day from the stream
A Dataflow Gen2 that refreshes on a schedule

questions.explanation: Eventhouses are the analytics engine for data in motion, queried in KQL or T-SQL, with seconds from data ingestion to insights.

questions.stem: A team writes PySpark and wants to stream events into a Delta table in a lakehouse, with a checkpoint so a restart carries on where it stopped. Which engine fits?

options.text: A KQL materialized view that keeps a copy of the stream for each restart
A pipeline copy activity that runs again after each failure
Spark Structured Streaming, writing in Delta format with a checkpointLocation
An eventstream, with a filter operator configured to resume from its last event

questions.explanation: In a lakehouse, Spark Structured Streaming writes with format("delta"), a checkpointLocation option and toTable, so the stream lands in a managed Delta table.

questions.stem: A Spark stream writes many small files to its Delta table. What does the guidance suggest?

options.text: Set a trigger interval, such as processingTime="1 minute", so data is written in fewer, larger writes
Switch the outputMode from append to complete, so each write replaces the table
Remove the checkpointLocation, so each microbatch starts again from scratch
Run the stream in several notebooks at once, so each writes a share of the files

questions.explanation: By default Spark processes each microbatch as soon as the previous one completes. A trigger interval gathers data over a period and writes it in fewer, larger operations.
